transcript:
This message comes from Capital One with the Capital One Saver Card.
Earn unlimited 3% cash back on dining and entertainment. Capital One.
What's in your wallet? Terms apply. Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, D.C., I'm Dale Willman. Speed disruptions are continuing with
Star Shield in Ukraine. NPR's Polina Litvinova reports from Kyiv that President Zelensky's
tech adviser says Ukraine is still experiencing restrictions on its use of Starlink.
Seribis Krasnoff wrote on social media that there are isolated cases where Starlink might
function beyond the limits. He added, though, this is "likely a result of SpaceX's algorithms
or specific usage conditions rather than actual removal of restrictions." Starlink is crucial for
Ukraine's military operations and defending against Russian airstrikes. Last week, without
warning, the country lost the ability to use Starlink for these critical functions.
And now Ukraine is seeking alternative satellite communications.
President Volodymyr Zelensky announced Ukraine and Finland agreed that Finnish tech giants Nokia
and Isai will help Ukraine to strengthen its satellite capabilities.
Polina Litvinova, NPR News, Kyiv. The Trump administration plans to exempt
some packaging and other products from tariffs on Canadian goods. And as Kevin Miller with
Maine Public Radio reports, the exemptions could help Senator Susan Collins' re-election bid.
Collins said the exemptions will benefit farmers in Maine and other states who rely on boxes,
crates, packaging, and specialized equipment from Canada. President Trump's trade war with Canada
is deeply unpopular in Maine because of the state's close economic ties with its neighbor to the north.
Collins opposes the tariffs and has campaigned on her ability to negotiate carve-outs from the Trump
administration. But her opponent in next month's election, Democrat Troy Jackson, has accused
Collins of failing to use her seniority and influence in D.C. to push back against Trump.
Maine's close Senate race is one of a handful that could determine control of the chamber.
For NPR News, I'm Kevin Miller. France is deploying 70,000 police to secure streets
during tomorrow's protest marches. As NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports,
there's a curfew for minors in several cities, including parts of Paris.
"The Louvre and several other major Paris museums will be closed Saturday. Many Paris shopkeepers,
still reeling from the destruction and violence of last weekend, have boarded up their stores.
In Lyon, Nice and Montpellier, marches have been banned for security reasons. In Paris,
authorities have diverted some protest routes away from shopping streets and public buildings
to limit possible damage. President Emmanuel Macron, who has been criticized for being absent
from the crisis, met with high school students for the first time to hear their grievances.
He said the government would work with them to find solutions. But critics say he has already
lost French youth. Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris. On Wall Street, stocks finished down
across the board. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 652 points. The Nasdaq down by 53 points.
And you're listening to NPR News.
President Trump says he is responsible for a lawsuit filed by the federal government over
Alaska's U.S. Senate race. The administration has filed the lawsuit in an attempt to block
certification of the race if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses. Another candidate with the
same name is also on the ballot. The state's Supreme Court has already rejected an effort
to remove the other Sullivan from the ballot. For generations, visitors to New York City have
climbed into a horse-drawn carriage for a postcard tour of Central Park. As Steve Kastenbaum reports,
the city council has now voted to ban them. People have been able to hire a horse-drawn
carriage for a ride through the park since 1858. If this ban survives legal challenges from the
driver's union, the popular tourist attraction will disappear in two years. City Council President
Julie Menon. They don't belong in an area that attracts 42 million people a year,
pulling a thousand pound carriage in record-breaking heat. New York's horse-drawn carriage
industry supports around 150 drivers. Under the legislation, the city would have to develop a
transition plan to help them find new jobs. Several other cities have passed similar bans
with the most recent one winning approval in Philadelphia. For NPR News, I'm Steve Kastenbaum
in New York. American gymnast Sky Blakely has won the all-around gold medal that happened
earlier today at the World Gymnastics Championships underway in the Netherlands. The 21-year-old
from Dallas put together four outstanding performances, including a set on uneven bars.
Blakely missed both the 2020 and the 2024 Olympics because of injuries. I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Ukraine still restricted in its use of Starlink satellite service, adviser says
Ukraine and Finland agree Nokia and Isai will help strengthen Ukraine's satellite capabilities
Trump administration plans tariff exemptions on some Canadian packaging and other products, benefiting Maine farmers
France deploys 70,000 police and bans some protest marches ahead of nationwide demonstrations
Stocks finish sharply lower, with the Dow down 652 points
Federal government sues over Alaska Senate race, seeking to block certification if Dan Sullivan loses
New York City Council votes to ban horse-drawn carriages from Central Park
Sky Blakely wins all-around gold at World Gymnastics Championships in the Netherlands
